title: Munir Frames 2025 India-Pakistan War as 'Battle of Ideologies'
excerpt: Pakistan's army chief marks the Marka-e-Haq anniversary with renewed two-nation rhetoric and unverified military claims
body:
On the first anniversary of the May 2025 India-Pakistan conflict, Pakistan's Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir stood before senior military leadership at GHQ Rawalpindi and reframed the four-day war in sweeping terms — not as a clash between states, but as a civilisational contest.

**What Munir said:**
Addressing a ceremony to mark 'Marka-e-Haq' — Islamabad's name for the conflict — Munir declared it 'a decisive battle between two ideologies,' not merely a traditional military engagement. He claimed Pakistan's strategy was *superior* to India's, alleged Pakistan struck 26 targets, and asserted that India sought a ceasefire through the United States. He provided no evidence for any of these claims. India has consistently maintained that the ceasefire understanding was reached directly between the two sides through military communication channels.

**Why this rhetoric matters now:**
Munir's framing echoes the provocative two-nation theory speech he delivered at the Overseas Pakistanis Convention in April 2025 — just days before the Pahalgam terror attack that killed 26 tourists and triggered India's Operation Sindoor. That operation struck nine terror infrastructure sites in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir. Analysts at the time noted Munir's ideological speeches had complicated Pakistan's diplomatic posture by undermining any narrative of restraint. Now, marking the anniversary with identical rhetoric signals that Rawalpindi views the conflict not as a crisis to be managed, but as a moment of identity to be celebrated.

**What to watch:**
Munir also signalled Pakistan's military buildup — citing Hangor-class submarines, a new Rocket Force, and fighter aircraft — framing future wars as 'multi-domain' conflicts; how New Delhi responds to this anniversary messaging will set the tone for bilateral tensions in the months ahead.
nri_angle: For Indian-Americans with family ties to India, Munir's decision to mark the conflict's anniversary with two-nation ideology rhetoric — rather than de-escalation signals — raises direct questions about the durability of the May 2025 ceasefire and the long-term security of the subcontinent.
author: Diaspora Desk
